verdict: Caution on Itanagar hospitality: lend only to owner-operated, cash-generating F&B and mid-market room assets with verified occupancy; avoid new-build banquet-led projects until the Yashshree supply is absorbed.
title: Itanagar Tourism, Hotels & Restaurants: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What the business physically is
**A hotel in Itanagar converts rooms, food and event space into daily cash, and the cash sits in the banquet calendar, not the room key.** Revenue comes from room nights, F&B covers and wedding/conference bookings; costs are largely fixed (staff, power, rent or EMI) so a single weak wedding season hits EBITDA hard. **Working capital is short and favourable** — guests pay at checkout, banquet advances come in weeks ahead — so the real risk is capex and debt service, not receivables. **Collect from customer** the actual room count, ARR, occupancy and banquet advance book; nothing in the sources gives Itanagar-specific operating numbers.

## What has changed now
**New supply is landing: Yashshree GD Garden Resort brings 45 rooms, a 6,000 sq ft banquet hall, 2,500 sq ft conference room, 800 sq ft boardroom and a 10,000 sq ft lawn on Jollang Road, Naharlagun [1][2].** That is a direct hit on the wedding and MICE cash that existing Itanagar hotels and banquet halls live on. **So when a proposal lands from an incumbent banquet or mid-market hotel, check its share of revenue from weddings and conferences; if it is above half, ask for the forward booking register and the last two seasons' event calendar.** Peer results are strong but national, not local: ITC Hotels Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue Rs 1,054 crore up 26 percent, EBITDA Rs 337 crore up 37 percent [4]; Leela's Q2 was 30 percent RevPAR growth, entirely ARR-led, on MICE demand [6]. **Read these as proof that branded MICE pricing works nationally, not as evidence about Itanagar.**

## Where the growth is
**Pursue the owner-operated restaurant and mid-market lodge serving business and government visitors, and the catering/banquet operator with a proven advance book.** These turn cash monthly and need modest capex. **Avoid greenfield five-star or large-banquet builds** — the new 45-room resort [1] will absorb the premium event demand first, and a second entrant has no pricing power. **If a borrower proposes a new banquet lawn or conference block, ask who their anchor wedding clients are and get signed advance contracts before sanction.**

## How to grow safely
**Structure against the cash cycle: sanction against verified banquet advances and monthly F&B collections, not projected occupancy.** Take **monthly** bank statements, GST returns and the banquet advance ledger; take **quarterly** occupancy and ARR. **Covenant a minimum DSCR from operating cash and a cap on further capex** until the Yashshree property's opening date and bookings are announced [1]. **If the borrower cannot show three months of steady collections, ask for a promoter guarantee and a cash sweep on banquet advances.**

## Early-warning signs
**Watch banquet advance cancellations, falling ARR without occupancy gain, and delayed staff or power payments.** A drop in wedding bookings after the new resort opens [1][2] is the first real signal. **If advances fall two months running, cut limits and re-price.** Rating commentary on hotel liquidity stresses cash flow from operations and promoter support [9]; apply the same test here. **Sources say little about Itanagar specifically — lean on first principles and these peers.**
watch: Two consecutive months of falling advances -> freeze fresh limits and re-price
Missed staff or power payments -> demand promoter infusion before next disbursal
ARR falls with flat occupancy -> shift to cash-collateralised lending
Opening date confirmed -> reassess incumbent event revenue share
